blocks.text: Cleanliness, as the saying goes, is next to godliness. Without the Sanitation department, church premises would quickly become a dumping ground. This unit isn't as conspicuous or celebrated as some others, but what it does - or fails to do - has an immediate effect on the atmosphere of worship, because God is holy. The unit is led by a Head of Sanitation, and any willing, humble-minded individual can be part of it.

items: Ensuring church premises or event venues are clean, neat, and tidy before, during, and after events.
Ensuring proper disposal of waste at designated places after thorough cleaning.
Regularly organising, maintaining, and enforcing sanitation regulations in the church.
Regularly cleaning toilets, bathrooms, offices, and other frequently used spaces.
Occasionally collaborating with ushers to arrange seats and furniture at event venues.

blocks.text: An intending sanitation worker needs to be:

items: Humble - a quiet, caring individual who doesn't work to be noticed.
Not easily nauseated - able to handle different types of waste, including toilets, without being sickened by the work.
Hygienic - for personal safety and health.
Ready to work unnoticed - this role doesn't attract celebration or instant praise, and isn't suited to those who need recognition for the smallest effort.
